question: The carrier as an air base (CRebaseToCarrierMission), carrying land units by air (CLoadOnPlaneCommand, CUnloadFromPlaneCommand), the paradrop (CParadropMission) and the air supply (CTransportSuppliesOrder).

structs.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission
structs.comment: The air order `rebase_to_carrier` (type 0x573): an air group made of carrier air groups only is given a ship of a fleet of its own country as its base, attached under the fleet in the order of battle, and flown to wherever that fleet is. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.
structs.evidence: RTTI: one base, CAirOrder at offset 0, one table at VA 0x15C6694 (40 slots). Slots 7, 11, 13, 14 and 15 are held by this table alone (vtable.py --holding).

structs.name: CParadropMission
structs.comment: The air order `paradrop` (type 0x570): fly the land units an air unit carries to a land province and drop them there. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.
structs.evidence: RTTI: one base, CAirOrder at offset 0, one table at VA 0x15C649C (40 slots). Slots 7, 11, 13, 14 and 15 are held by this table alone.

structs.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder
structs.comment: The air order `transport_supplies` (Air Supply): carry supplies and fuel from the unit's base province to a friendly province of the mission's area that is short of them. Driven by CAirOrder::UpdateBombing like the strike missions. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.
structs.evidence: RTTI: one base, CAirOrder at offset 0, one table at VA 0x15C67E4 (40 slots). Slots 7, 11, 13, 14, 15, 37 and 39 are held by this table alone.

structs.name: CLoadOnPlaneCommand
structs.comment: Command type 0x56E: put a land unit aboard an air unit (transport planes). Keys `unit` and `air`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.
structs.evidence: RTTI: one base, CCommand at offset 0, table VA 0x15C91DC (15 slots). Size: its slot 13 (Clone, 0x5E4AD0) allocates 0x8C bytes (`push 0x8c; call operator new`) and copy-constructs into it.

structs.name: CUnloadFromPlaneCommand
structs.comment: Command type 0x56F: take a land unit off the air unit carrying it. Key `unit` (its LoadKey is the body CDisbandCommand::LoadKey, shared). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.
structs.evidence: RTTI: one base, CCommand at offset 0, table VA 0x15C919C (15 slots). Size: slot 13 (Clone, 0x5E43A0) allocates 100 = 0x64 bytes and copies +0x3C..+0x48 into it.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11. True where FindCarrierWithRoom (0xA8470) finds, for this air unit, a fleet with a carrier that has room among the units of the order's province (CMapProvince +0x2B8) or, where that finds none and the province has a port (+0x354), among the fleets in its port (CPort +8); and the unit is an air unit (slot 17) whose every wing is a carrier air group (CUnit_AllSubUnitsAreCag). No test of range, war, friendship or the carrier's being at sea or in port. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x593050..0x5930A7 end to end, 24 instructions, two bare `ret`. The list handed in EAX is `lea eax,[ebx+0x2b8]` then `lea eax,[ebx+8]` with ebx = province->+0x354. `[eax+0x44]` is CUnit slot 17, IsAir in the record. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: FindCarrierWithRoom answering something other than a fleet - it returns the list element only after slot 16 (IsNaval) is true for it.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13, run when the order is given. Finds the fleet as MayBeGiven does and keeps its object id in the order (+0x84 type, +0x88 id; the save key `carrier_target`). Then walks the fleet's ships (CUnit +0x38) in order for the first with carrier_size (CSubUnitDefinition +0x190) above nought whose air groups aboard (the list at CShip +0xDC) hold, counted in wings (CUnit +0x40 regiments_count, summed) together with this unit's wings, no more than carrier_size / 1000; on that ship: the unit is taken off its old base's list (CList_RemoveNode), its base (CUnit +0x98) becomes the CUnitBaseCarrier embedded in the ship at +0xD8, CUnitBase::AddUnit puts it on the ship's list, and CUnit_AttachToParent(unit, the fleet) hangs it under the fleet in the order of battle. Last, FlyToCarrier (0x193910) - also where no ship had room. **So the base changes the moment the order is given**, as CRebaseAirOrder's does. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5930B0..0x593286 off the listing. The divide by 1000 is `mov eax,0x10624dd3; imul edi; sar edx,6` on carrier_size at 0x5931FC; the comparison `cmp [esp+0x10], ecx; jg next ship` at 0x59320D takes a ship when the sum is at most that. The base object is `add esi, 0xd8` on the ship at 0x593246, stored at unit+0x98 at 0x59324C - and CShip's constructor (0x5ADB60) writes CUnitBaseCarrier's vftable 0x15C7A38 at +0xD8 and the ship at +0xF0, which is the base's +0x18 the record calls `ship`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: CUnit +0x40 not being the wing count on an air unit - it is the regiments CList's count, recorded.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14, every hour. Looks the fleet up again by the id it kept and caches it at +0x80: no such fleet, done; no base, done. A unit in a battle (+0x11C), a bombing (+0x110) or with a path (+0x140) goes on. Otherwise: at its own base (CUnit_IsAtOwnBase - for a carrier base, in the fleet's province with the fleet in no battle), done; elsewhere, FlyToCarrier again and it goes on. It never calls CAirOrder::IsActive, so **no range is ever measured on the way**. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x593290..0x59332A. FindPersistentById on {+0x84,+0x88}, `add eax,-8` and the store at +0x80 (0x5932DC); `call 0x5cdc30` then `jne` to the false exit at 0x59331C. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a caller of slot 14 that also asks CAirOrder::IsActive for this class - CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat calls slot 14 alone.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::FlyToCarrier
addresses.comment: Not a slot. The unit is given the way from where it is to the province the fleet is in now (CPathFind::Find, SetUnitPath); with a way found, the light at its hour of arrival is judged as the strike missions judge it (the order's `time`, +0x30: 0 refuses an arrival at night and 1 one by day) - where it would arrive in the wrong light, a unit standing in its base's province has its movement cancelled and any other is told to return to base. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x593910..0x593A42 (bare `ret`; the `ret 8` after it belong to LoadKey at 0x593A50). The target is `[fleet+0x130]` after FindPersistentById on {+0x84,+0x88}. The light test is the same CUnit::NextArrivalHour / IsNightAtTick / `+0x30 == 0 && night || +0x30 == 1 && day` shape the record has for CAirOrder::UpdateBombing. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: another caller passing an order of a different class - its two callers are this class's slots 13 and 14.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::Describe
addresses.comment: Slot 15, the order's line in the unit panel: REBASE_TO_CAG_MISSION_SHORT_DESC 'Rebase to Carrier ($TYPE$)' with TYPE STRAT_BOMB_RETURNING 'Returning' where return_to_base is set, else STRAT_BOMB_WAITING 'Resting' in its base's province, else PARA_FLYING 'Flying' in no battle and no bombing, else CAG_FIGHTING 'Fighting'. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.evidence: The five key strings are pushed in this body (0x593330..0x5937D0, `ret 4`); the order of the tests is read off the decompilation and the branches on +0x18, +0x130 against the base's slot 0, +0x11C and +0x110. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the localisation using a different key - all five are in the install's CSVs.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::GetDescription
addresses.comment: Slot 7: REB_CAG_MISSION_DESC, 'Rebasing aircraft to a carrier, which then becomes that air unit's base.'
addresses.evidence: `assign("REB_CAG_MISSION_DESC", 0x14)`, GetText, Render; `ret 4`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing short of a second key in the body, and there is none.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11: the order's province is land (its template's is_land, CProvinceTemplate +0x22). Nothing else - not range, not war, not that anything is aboard. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
addresses.evidence: The whole body: `mov eax,[ecx+0xc]; mov ecx,[eax+0xd4]; cmp byte [ecx+0x22],0; setne al; ret`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing; it is five instructions.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13: `push ecx; call CParadropMission::TakeOff; ret`.
addresses.evidence: Three instructions at 0x590920. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::TakeOff
addresses.comment: What starts a drop, from slot 13 and from slot 14 every hour the unit is not yet over its target. Out of fuel (CUnit +0x100 zero) or unfit to fly (slot 25, CAirOrder::IsFitToFly): told to return to base. Before the order's start hour (+0x28): nothing. Then, with `enemy` = the target's controller at war with the air unit's owner (CCountry::IsEnemy): for each unit it carries (CUnit +0x2E4), where `enemy` and that unit's attack delay (CUnit +0xD4) is running, nothing - it waits; and for each brigade of each, organisation x 1000 / maximum organisation (a maximum of 0 counts as -1) under PARATROOP_MISSION_ORG_REQ (military +0xAC, 0.95), nothing - it waits. Otherwise the way to the target (CPathFind::Find, SetUnitPath) and the light at the hour of arrival judged as FlyToCarrier does; the wrong light leaves a unit at its base with its movement cancelled and sends any other home. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x590930..0x590C51 off the listing, three `ret 4`. IsEnemy at 0x590A2B with ESI = countries[target->controller_id], EDX = &unit->owner, EDI = target, per its recorded register convention. The org requirement is `[defines->military + 0xAC]` at 0x590A3F, which definesMap.py maps to PARATROOP_MISSION_ORG_REQ; the brigade loop compares with `jl` to the plain exit at 0x590B18. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the wait arms falling through to the path - both `jg`/`jl` go to 0x590C40, the epilogue.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14, every hour. No base: done. In a battle, a bombing or with a path: goes on. At its own base with nothing aboard (+0x2EC): done. Before the start hour: goes on. Not in the target province: TakeOff again, goes on. **Over the target: the drop** - CAir::DropCarried; each wing's organisation (+0x60) x PARATROOP_DROP_ORG_MULT_PLANE (military +0xA8, 0.01) / 1000, not under 0; told to return to base; and the first time only (byte +0x80, saved as `message`), where the target's controller is the player and the air unit's owner is at war with the player, the message PARATROOPEDUS with ENEMY the owner's name and PROV the province's. Never asks CAirOrder::IsActive, so no range is measured. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x590C60..0x590F10 and the epilogue at 0x5913B2 off the listing. The organisation product is `__allmul(org, mult)` then `__alldiv(,1000)` with `cmovl eax, 0` at 0x590E0E. The message gate: `cmp [province+0x338], [state+0xC34]` (the player's id) at 0x590EEF, then 0x42F1B0 (IsEnemy, Lua overload) on the owner's country with the player's tag; the key and its two variables are pushed at 0x590F*-0x5911*. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the byte +0x80 being set elsewhere - its only other users are the save and LoadKey (`message`).

addresses.name: CParadropMission::Describe
addresses.comment: Slot 15: PARADROP_MISSION_SHORT_DESC 'Airborne Assault ($TYPE$}' (the brace is the localisation's) with TYPE STRAT_BOMB_WAITING 'Resting' while unfit to fly (slot 25), STRAT_BOMB_RETURNING 'Returning' with return_to_base set, 'Resting' in its base's province, PARA_FLYING 'Flying' in no battle and no bombing, CAG_FIGHTING 'Fighting' otherwise.
addresses.evidence: Key strings pushed in 0x5913D0..0x5919A0 (`ret 4`); order of the tests from the decompilation and the branches on slot 25 (+0x64), +0x18, +0x130/base slot 0, +0x11C, +0x110. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a localisation key missing from the CSVs - all present.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::GetDescription
addresses.comment: Slot 7: PARA_MISSION_DESC, 'Perform an airborne assault on a province, dropping paratroopers on the target.'
addresses.evidence: `assign("PARA_MISSION_DESC", 0x11)`; `ret 4`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11: the order's province is land and the unit's definition has a transport_capability (CSubUnitDefinition +0x144, the air file's `transport_capability`) above nought.
addresses.evidence: The whole body, 0x595300..0x595325. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13: a five-byte `jmp CAirOrder::UpdateBombing` (0x18A2E0). Ghidra decompiles it as UpdateBombing's whole body (labels LAB_0058a46b and the rest give it away). So the air supply is given its target, its way and its light test by the strike missions' hour.
addresses.evidence: `jmp 0x58a2e0` at 0x595480 followed by int3. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14, every hour. No base: done. With a target (+0x68): standing in it, the cargo is delivered - the target's pool (CMapProvince +0x15C) gains the supplies (+0x84) and the fuel (+0x80) carried, and cargo and target are cleared; elsewhere, at its own base: cap = AIR_SUPPLY_FACTOR (military +0x230, 0.5) x transport_capability / 1000; where no supplies are aboard, supplies = the target's drawn less its throughput today where that is above nought, at most cap, **counted into the base province's drawn**, then at most the base province's pool, and taken out of it; fuel the same, after. Then: at its own base with a target and nothing aboard, it goes on without moving; otherwise CAirOrder::UpdateBombing, and CAirOrder::IsActive answers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.4.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x595490..0x595668 off the listing; it ends `jmp 0x58a5e0` (CAirOrder::IsActive) after `call 0x58a2e0`. +0x164 and +0x168 are pool.supplies and pool.fuel (CMapProvince +0x15C pool, CGoodsPool +8/+0xC); +0x1A8 drawn_ptr and +0x1F8 throughput_ptr are recorded. The cap is `imul [defines->military+0x230]` with transport_capability then `__alldiv(,1000)`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x84/+0x80 being other than supplies/fuel - the save writes +0x84 under token 0x469 and +0x80 under 0x46C, and LoadKey reads `supplies` and `fuel` back into them.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::Describe
addresses.comment: Slot 15: TRANS_SUP_MISSION_SHORT_DESC 'Air Supply ($TYPE$)' with TYPE TS_RETURNING 'Returning' with return_to_base set, TS_WAITING 'Waiting' at its own base with no path, TS_SUPPLYING 'Flying' otherwise.
addresses.evidence: Key strings pushed in 0x595670..0x595B0F (`ret 4`); tests on +0x18, CUnit_IsAtOwnBase and +0x140. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing short of another key.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::GetDescription
addresses.comment: Slot 7: TRANS_SUP_MISSION_DESC, 'Deliver supplies through the air to any troops needing them.'
addresses.evidence: `assign("TRANS_SUP_MISSION_DESC", 0x16)`; `ret 4`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::IsProvinceAllowed
addresses.comment: Slot 37: CCountry::IsFriend(the province's controller, the unit's owner, true) - the controller counts the unit's country a friend, military access counting.
addresses.evidence: 0x595BF0..0x595C32: `countries[province->+0x338]`, `push 1; push &unit->owner; call 0x4ef7c0`; `ret 4`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39, asked by CAirOrder::UpdateBombing at the base for a target. Over the mission's area list (CAirOrder +0x44) in order, provinces slot 37 allows: the first is taken whatever it lacks; every later one replaces it where (drawn.fuel - throughput.fuel) + (drawn.supplies - throughput.supplies) is above nought. **So the last short province of the list wins, and with none short after the first, the first.** Null where none is allowed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.4.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x595C40..0x595CAF: `cmp [ebp-4],0; je take` at 0x595C73 takes the first, and the sum's `jle skip` at 0x595C9A guards every later replacement. Ghidra's decompilation drops the assignment. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing; it is 28 instructions.

addresses.name: CLoadOnPlaneCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6. Resolves `unit` (+0x40/+0x44 into +0x3C) and `air` (+0x68/+0x6C into +0x64). Where the unit is a land unit (slot 15) not already aboard a plane (CArmy +0x304): CAir::Board(air, unit); CUnit::EnterProvince(unit, the province it is in), which leaves it where it is; and where it was selected the selection is cleared and the air unit selected unless it already was. In every case the land unit's order then becomes a null order (CreateOrder(0x18D) through CUnit::SetOrder - twice where it boarded, once where it did not). No test here of where either unit is, nor of what IsValid tests. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.2.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5E4750..0x5E49E9 off the listing, bare `ret`. CAir::Board at 0x5E4812 with ESI = air->slot13() (ReturnThis for a CAir) and EDI = the unit; EnterProvince at 0x5E4820 with ECX = EDI and `push [edi+0x130]`; the two `push 0x18d; call 0x583aa0; call 0x5cd9e0` at 0x5E49AC and 0x5E49C3, the first skipped by the not-a-land-unit / already-aboard jumps to 0x5E49C1. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: CUnit::SetOrder's register `this` being another unit - EAX = EDI at both sites.

addresses.name: CLoadOnPlaneCommand::IsValid
addresses.comment: Slot 14: both ids resolve, and CAir::MayLoad(air, unit).
addresses.evidence: 0x5E4BF0..0x5E4CA1: two FindPersistentById, then `push land; push air->slot13(); call 0x5d07f0`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CLoadOnPlaneCommand::GetTypeId
addresses.comment: Slot 7: 0x56E.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax, 0x56e; ret`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CLoadOnPlaneCommand::Clone
addresses.comment: Slot 13: operator new 0x8C and a copy through 0x5E4B40. `ret 0x1C`, the string by value as the other commands' Clone.
addresses.evidence: 0x5E4AD0..0x5E4B3B, `ret 0x1c`; the record's other Clone bodies (CHourlyTickCommand, CExecuteDecisionCommand) have the same shape. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CUnloadFromPlaneCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6: CAir::ReleaseCarried(the unit's plane, false) - no supplies, but a CheckForCombat in the province - and where the unit is selected it is taken out of its province's list and put back (CMapProvince::RemoveUnit / AddUnit), which redraws its counter. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.2.
addresses.evidence: 0x5E4300..0x5E4389: `push 0; push [unit->slot9()+0x304]; mov edi, esi; call 0x5d0990`, then `cmp byte [esi+4],0` and the two province calls. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CUnloadFromPlaneCommand::IsValid
addresses.comment: Slot 14: the unit resolves; the province it is in is land; it is aboard a plane (CArmy +0x304); and that plane is at its own base (CUnit_IsAtOwnBase). This is UW_UNLOAD_PLANE_BASE_ONLY's 'You can only unload at an airbase.'
addresses.evidence: 0x5E4450..0x5E4521: `[unit+0x130]->+0xD4->+0x22`, `cmp [unit->slot9()+0x304],0`, `mov esi,[...+0x304]; call 0x5cdc30`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CUnloadFromPlaneCommand::GetTypeId
addresses.comment: Slot 7: 0x56F.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax, 0x56f; ret`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CUnloadFromPlaneCommand::Clone
addresses.comment: Slot 13: operator new 0x64, CCommand's constructor, the vftable, +0x3C..+0x44 and the string at +0x48 copied. Ghidra's own RTTI pass calls it the constructor; it is the clone. `ret 0x1C`.
addresses.evidence: 0x5E43A0..0x5E4445, `ret 0x1c`, held at slot 13 of CUnloadFromPlaneCommand's table alone. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CAir::MayLoad
addresses.comment: Whether a land unit may board an air unit, in order: one owner (+0x128); the air unit in no battle (+0x11C), with no path (+0x140), not retreating (+0x158), at its own base (CUnit_IsAtOwnBase) and with a base; the land unit's attack delay (CUnit +0xD4) not running; the base province's air base (CMapProvince +0x304) at a working level of at least 1 (+0x24 >= 1000); every brigade can_paradrop (CSubUnitDefinition +0x38) and at organisation x 1000 / maximum (0 counts as -1) of at least PARATROOP_MISSION_ORG_REQ (military +0xAC, 0.95); and SumTransportWeight(what the air unit carries) + the land unit's transport_weight / 1000 at most its transport_capability / 1000. **Where the land unit stands is not asked.** The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.2.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5D07F0..0x5D091D end to end, one `ret 8`; the call site 0x5E4C86/0x5E4C90 pushes the land unit first and the air unit last, so air is stack:4. 0x5C7510 and 0x5C74F0 are read (definition +0x10C and +0x144, each /1000 truncated toward nought). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a location test elsewhere on the path to Execute - IsValid calls nothing else and Execute tests only slot 15 and +0x304.

addresses.name: CAir::Board
addresses.comment: Puts a land unit aboard an air unit: the unit's +0x304 = the air unit, its +0x2E8 = 0 (recorded as CArmy ai_param_a), and it is appended to the air unit's list at +0x2E4 (first +0x2E4, last +0x2E8, count +0x2EC). Called by CLoadOnPlaneCommand::Execute and by CAir::LoadKey for a `division` block inside an `air` block - which is how a save keeps a unit aboard a plane. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 0x5D0920..0x5D0985, two bare `ret`, nothing on the stack; ESI and EDI read uninitialised at entry; callers 0x5D05E4 (CAir::LoadKey) and 0x5E4812. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CAir::ReleaseCarried
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAir::ReleaseCarried(CAir* air@stack:4, bool parachuted@stack:8, CArmy* unit@EDI)
addresses.comment: Lets go of a land unit an air unit carries: the unit's +0x304 and +0x2E8 are zeroed and it is taken off the air unit's list (+0x2E4); **with `parachuted` set**, CUnit::CarrySupplies(unit, its province, true, true) - PARASUPPLYPOOL_DAYS of what it uses, taken from the pool of the land province it last walked out of (CUnit +0x134) where it has one, else from its owner's stockpile; and **always** CCombatManager::CheckForCombat(unit, its province). Two callers: CAir::DropCarried (parachuted) and CUnloadFromPlaneCommand::Execute (not). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, sections D.2 and D.3.
addresses.revises: Was `inferred` with no signature, and its comment made CheckForCombat look conditional on the byte and said a dropped unit's supplies come 'out of its country's stockpile'. CheckForCombat is unconditional (0x5D09FD is reached from both arms of the `cmp cl,bl` at 0x5D09E9). And CarrySupplies takes from the pool of the unit's previous province where that is land (0x5BEDCC..0x5BEDE7, the `+0x134` test comes before and regardless of the from-stockpile byte, which only guards the arm with no previous province) - a paratrooper's previous province is the one it last stepped out of on foot, since neither boarding nor the plane's moves write +0x134. Signature added.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5D0990..0x5D0A98, `ret 8`; the air unit is `[ebp+8]` (`add esi,0x2e4` at 0x5D09B9), the byte `[ebp+0xC]`, the unit EDI (`cmp [eax],edi` in the list walk, and both callers set EDI before the call: 0x5D0B0A, 0x5E435F). +0x134's writers: AdvanceMovement (three), the constructors and the loaders - fieldchain over 0x5A..0x5E. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a write of +0x134 in CUnit::EnterProvince, which the passenger's moves go through - none of the nine writers is in 0x5BEFD0's extent.

addresses.name: CAir::DropCarried
addresses.comment: The drop. `hostile` = CCountry::IsEnemy(the air unit's owner, the controller of the province it is in). For each unit it carries, in order: its byte +0x97 (`was_paradropped`) = hostile; where hostile, CUnit::StartAttackDelay (PARATROOP_MISSION_DELAY in place of UNIT_ATTACK_DELAY); then CAir::ReleaseCarried(air, true). One caller, CParadropMission::IsActive. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5D0AA0..0x5D0B21, `ret 4`. IsEnemy at 0x5D0ADA with ESI = countries[air->owner_id], EDX = &province->controller (+0x334), EDI = the province; `mov [esi+0x97], al` at 0x5D0AF6; StartAttackDelay takes the unit in ESI. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: FindCarrierWithRoom
addresses.comment: The first unit of a list of units that is a fleet (slot 16) of the air unit's owner (+0x128) and has a ship with carrier_size above nought whose air groups aboard (CShip +0xDC), counted in wings (+0x40), plus the air unit's wings, are at most carrier_size / 1000. Null where none. Asked of a province's units and of its port's fleets by CRebaseToCarrierMission's MayBeGiven and Start, and by the air orders window (0x7466D2, 0x7466E9). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x4A8470..0x4A852E, `ret 4` at both exits; EAX holds the list's head field at entry (`mov eax,[eax]`). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing; the six callers set EAX with a `lea` of a list field.

addresses.name: CUnit_AttachToParent
addresses.comment: Hangs a unit under another in the order of battle: nothing unless they have one owner (+0x128) and the parent's oob_level (+0x1F4) is below the child's; the child leaves its old parent (CUnit_LeaveParent, notifying the AI where the AI agents differ); it is appended to the parent's children (+0x1E4) and its parent (+0x1E0) set; an AI agent of its own is let go; the nearest AI agent above it is marked. A fleet is level 5 and an air unit 6 (their constructors, 0x5CEE5F and 0x5D048E), so an air group goes under a fleet. 17 callers. The name is ours; the AI parts and the log line inside were not read closely.
addresses.evidence: Read the gates and list append of 0x5B9760..0x5B9A21 (`ret 8`); `cmp [edi+0x1f4], [ebx+0x1f4]; jge exit` at 0x5B97A5 and the node {child, last, 0, 0} appended at parent+0x1E4..+0x1EC, `mov [ebx+0x1e0], edi`. Inferred only because the AI-agent tail was taken from the decompilation. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the stack order - CRebaseToCarrierMission::Start pushes the fleet and then the unit, so the unit is stack:4.

addresses.name: CGameState::DisposeSubUnit
addresses.comment: What is done with a ship, wing or brigade that is taken out of its unit for good. A ship (slot 10) whose byte +0xF4 is set (CShip's constructor sets it) has, **for each air group based on it** (CShip +0xDC): the group taken off the ship's list, its base (+0x98) cleared, a fresh null order put in (its slot 13 called), CAir::CheckBase (the nearest of its country's air bases in a straight line) and CUnit::EnterProvince where it is; and the ship is put on the game state's list at +0x20 rather than freed. Anything else is deleted at once. Called by CUnit::RemoveSpentSubUnits (a ship sunk) and by CGameState::RemoveUnit (a whole unit removed), among six. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x684CE0..0x684E3C off the listing, three `ret 8`. `state` is inferred from the two callers read: RemoveSpentSubUnits pushes the value it has just stored in g_CCurrentGameState (0x5C41C1..0x5C41D2), RemoveUnit its own `this`. What +0x20 holds afterwards and who frees it were not read. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the byte +0xF4 being cleared before a sinking - its writers were not looked for beyond the constructor.

addresses.name: CUnit_TransportCapability
addresses.comment: `unit->CSubUnitDefinitionPtr (+0xC8)->+0x144 / 1000`, truncated toward nought - how much an air unit (or a fleet) may carry, in whole weight units. One caller, CAir::MayLoad.
addresses.evidence: The whole body, 0x5C74F0..0x5C750D. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CUnit_TransportWeight
addresses.comment: `unit->CSubUnitDefinitionPtr (+0xC8)->+0x10C / 1000`, truncated - a land unit's transport_weight, the sum over its brigades, in whole units. Three callers: CAir::MayLoad and two at 0x6C6BB5 / 0x6C6F06 (not read).
addresses.evidence: The whole body, 0x5C7510..0x5C752D. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing.

addresses.name: CUnit_IsAtOwnBase
addresses.comment: **Whether a unit is at its own base, ready.** False with no base (+0x98) or where the base's slot 0 - its province - is not the province the unit is in (+0x130). For a carrier base (slot 1, IsCarrier), whose slot 0 answers the province the carrier's fleet is in, false again while that fleet (CUnitBaseCarrier +0x18 -> CShip +0xB0) is in a battle (+0x11C) or a bombing (+0x110). So an air group aboard a carrier is 'at base' where the fleet is and only while the fleet is not fighting. 58 callers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
addresses.revises: Was `likely`, with its third clause's object 'not identified'. The CUnitBaseCarrier +0x18 field record had since identified it as the carrier ship, and CUnitBaseCarrier's slot 0 (0x5D5570) is read here: it answers the ship's fleet's current province (provinces[0] where there is no ship or no fleet). Comment rewritten to say what the three clauses mean; the return placed in AL (`) @AL`), name unchanged.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x5CDC30..0x5CDC88 again (28 instructions) and the carrier base's slot 0, 0x5D5570..0x5D56C7: `[ecx+0x18]` -> `+0xB0` -> `+0x130`, with the provinces[0] fallback through g_CCurrentGameState +0xB8C. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: CUnitBaseCarrier slot 0 being reached for a land base - its table 0x15C7A38 is written only in CShip's constructor and four places that rebuild a ship.

addresses.name: CUnit_AllSubUnitsAreCag
addresses.comment: True where every wing of the unit is a carrier air group (CSubUnitDefinition +0x32, `is_cag`) and it has at least one. The gate on CRebaseToCarrierMission::MayBeGiven, and in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits on the carrier_protection order (0x4CDF89).
addresses.revises: Was `inferred`, resting on +0x32 being is_cag. The Lua API settles that: CSubUnitDefinition::IsCag reads +0x32 (bicelib_findings.json, the luabind half). Confidence raised; the comment adds the rebase-to-carrier caller; the return placed in AL.
addresses.evidence: The Lua registration of CSubUnitDefinition::IsCag on +0x32, and `is_cag = yes` in units/cag.txt and tfh/units/cag.txt alone. The call at 0x593093 is the new caller. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the luabind name being on a folded getter of another offset - it reads +0x32.

struct_fields.name: was_paradropped
struct_fields.comment: **Set on a land unit dropped by a paradrop into a province whose controller is at war with the dropper** (CAir::DropCarried, 0x5D0AF6 - the only writer but the constructor's zero), and saved as `was_paradropped` only where set. While it is set: CUnit::StartAttackDelay uses PARATROOP_MISSION_DELAY; CCombat::GetCombatWidth counts no paratrooper after the first; BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY applies (PARADROP_PENALTY + trait paradrop_mission, FINDINGS-combatmods.md); and BM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES does not. CUnit::UpdateHourly clears it the first hour the unit is in no battle and multiplies every brigade's organisation by PARATROOP_DROP_ORG_MULT (military +0xA4, 0.66) / 1000. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
struct_fields.revises: Name `paradrop_org_pending` -> `was_paradropped`, the game's own save key for it; type unchanged. The old comment had one reader and said its writer was not looked for: the writer is CAir::DropCarried, and it has four more readers than the organisation step, all in battle.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain.py --field 0x97 gives 13 sites; the CUnit ones are the writer 0x5D0AF6, the constructor 0x5B50DC, readers 0x569869 (BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY), 0x56A6CB (CLandCombatant slot 19, skips lack of supplies), 0x56BD12/0x56BD3F (GetCombatWidth), 0x5B9C98/0x5B9CA1 (UpdateHourly) and 0x5BAE29 (StartAttackDelay); the rest are stack frames. The save key: CUnit::LoadKey's case 0x5A2 at 0x5B7D02 is `add ebx,0x8f; push ebx; call ParseBool`, ebx being the unit's CPersistent at +8, so +0x8F + 8 = +0x97; the save at 0x5B8A36 writes token 0x5A2 from `[ebx+0x8f]` only when non-zero. saveTokens.py: 1442 = was_paradropped.

struct_fields.name: carried_by_air
struct_fields.comment: The air unit carrying this land unit, or null. Set by CAir::Board, cleared by CAir::ReleaseCarried. While set: the unit moves with the plane (CUnit::EnterProvince of an air unit enters each passenger into the same province), is never engaged (CUnit::CanEngage), is not reinforced (CanReinforce), is shown with the red cross of a unit that may not act (CUnit::IsFreeToAct), and draws its supplies at the plane's base (CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel). The sibling of +0x300 carried_by (a fleet). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.2.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x5D092A (Board, the air unit in ESI), 0x5D09BF (ReleaseCarried, zero) and 0x5CDF08 (a transfer of carried units between two units, 0x5CDC90, not read); read at 0x5E47F5, 0x5E44F1, 0x5E4356, 0x5C04A6/0x5C04E8 (CanEngage), 0x5C5AFE (IsFreeToAct), 0x5BBC90 (ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel), 0x5BF304 (EnterProvince), always on the object a unit's slot 9 answers - ReturnThis for a CArmy. Other +0x304 sites are CMapProvince's air_base (trap 12). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a write of a non-CAir there - both writers store the air unit.
